figures.caption: The seven-step systematic approach to a drug information request.
figures.alt: Seven numbered boxes in two rows joined by arrows: requester, background, real question, classify, search, answer, follow up and document. Step 3, the real question, is highlighted as the step most often skipped.

figures.caption: The evidence pyramid: stronger designs control bias better.
figures.alt: A six-level pyramid. From the base upward: case reports and expert opinion; case series and cross-sectional studies; case-control studies; cohort studies; randomised controlled trials; systematic reviews and meta-analyses at the top.

figures.caption: Managing a suspected adverse drug reaction, starting with the patient.
figures.alt: Five boxes in a vertical flow: patient first (stop, treat, monitor, escalate); evaluate (history, severity, seriousness); causality (WHO-UMC or Naranjo); record and report (EPVC); prevent (education, DTC review, regulator).
